Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results ​ ◾ Revenues of $1.58 billion, net loss of $320.1 million includes $286.7 million of goodwill impairment ◾ Adjusted EBITDA (1) of $36.0 million includes the unfavorable impact of $12.7 million of F&I chargeback liability adjustments ◾ Company accelerates cost actions; the Company’s efficiency program now totals over $150 million of anticipated annualized savings ◾ Fourth quarter 2026 SG&A expected to decline by more than $50 million year over year ◾ Good Sam Services and Plans gross margin expands 567 basis points to 62.3% ​ LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – November 2, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Camping World Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: CWH) (“CWH” or, collectively with its subsidiaries, the “Company” or “Camping World”), America’s Largest Recreational Vehicle Dealer, today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Matthew Wagner, Chief Executive Officer and President of CWH, stated, “Our team did a tremendous amount of work in the third quarter to position the Company for the future. We built on our inventory discipline from the first half and entered the fourth quarter with our lowest mix of prior model year new units in five years. We grew our new vehicle average selling price on a richer mix of fifth wheels and motorized units, sequentially improved used vehicle gross margins and GPU (2) , expanded Good Sam Services and Plans gross margins, and reduced our SG&A by $24 million in the quarter.” Mr. Wagner continued, “As signals emerged over the summer that new vehicle gross margins across the industry were likely to remain under greater pressure than we had anticipated, we moved swiftly to further optimize our cost structure. We accelerated elements of our previously announced $100 million efficiency program and implemented additional reductions amounting to over $50 million of anticipated incremental annualized savings. We enter the fourth quarter with a cost base that we believe is rebuilt for the current market backdrop and a team focused on the variables we can control.” Balance Sheet and Cash Flow At the end of the third quarter of 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $263.8 million. Total outstanding long-term debt was $1.423 billion. The Company’s Net Debt (1) decreased $97.8 million, or 7.0%, at the end of the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. Tom Kirn, Chief Financial Officer of CWH, commented, “Operating cash flow year to date was $488.0 million, we reduced total inventory by $343 million from year end and had floor plan capacity of $823 million. In August, we amended and extended our M&T real estate facility to 2031, and we continue to evaluate alternatives to potentially refinance our Senior Secured Credit Facilities with the goal of increasing our financial flexibility.” (1) Adjusted EBITDA and Net Debt are non-GAAP measures. For a reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, see the “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” section later in this press release. (2) Gross profit per unit (“GPU”). ​ Outlook As previously disclosed (3) , the Company expects full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to be below the low end of its previously communicated range of $230 million to $270 million. Currently, the Company is not providing additional full-year 2026 guidance and the Company intends to discuss its framework for 2027 in connection with its fourth quarter results. Mr. Wagner concluded, “The industry is planning for 2027 unit sales to be comparable to 2026, but we are building our plans around more conservative assumptions. With a cost base that we believe is on track to be more than $150 million lighter on an annualized basis by 2028, the largest used RV business in the industry, and a Good Sam business that compounds through the cycle, we believe we are positioned to deliver a step change in our earnings profile when the market turns.” (3) Disclosed in Item 7.01 of the Company’s Form 8-K furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission on October 5, 2026. 1 ​ Third Quarter Operating Highlights (4) ● Revenue was $1.6 billion for the third quarter, a decrease of $223.2 million, or 12.4%. ● New vehicle revenue was $638.9 million for the third quarter, a decrease of $127.9 million, or 16.7%, and new vehicle unit sales were 15,126 units, a decrease of 5,160 units, or 25.4%. Used vehicle revenue was $518.5 million for the third quarter, a decrease of $70.6 million, or 12.0%, and used vehicle unit sales were 17,176 units, a decrease of 1,518 units, or 8.1%. Combined new and used vehicle unit sales were 32,302, a decrease of 6,678 units, or 17.1%. ● Average selling price of new vehicles sold increased 11.7%, and average selling price of used vehicles sold decreased 4.2%. ● Same store new vehicle unit sales decreased 26.4% for the third quarter and same store used vehicle unit sales decreased 8.6%. Combined same store new and used vehicle unit sales decreased 17.8%. ● New vehicle gross margin was 10.2%, a decrease of 252 basis points, driven primarily by the 15.0% increase in the average cost per new vehicle sold, partially offset by the 11.7% increase in the average selling price per new vehicle sold. Used vehicle gross margin was 18.0%, a decrease of 36 basis points, primarily due to a 4.2% decrease in the average selling price per used vehicle sold, partially offset by a 3.8% decrease in the average cost per used vehicle sold. ● Products, service and other revenue was $209.0 million, a slight increase of $0.4 million, or 0.2%. Products, service and other gross margin was 38.3%, a decrease of 690 basis points, primarily due to a 12.8% increase in products, service and other costs applicable to revenue driven by higher service volume that was billed at lower average labor rates for basic installation and maintenance services. ● Finance and insurance, net was $147.5 million, a decrease of $30.8 million, or 17.3%, driven by a 17.1% decrease in total vehicle unit sales, which resulted in fewer contracts sold, and a $12.7 million unfavorable adjustment to variable consideration for chargebacks based on updates to the actuarial analysis of our chargeback liabilities, compared to a $3.7 million unfavorable chargeback adjustment in the prior year. ● Good Sam Club revenue was $19.0 million, an increase of $8.2 million, or 75.6%, driven by (i) increased co-branded credit card revenue from a revised partner agreement that resulted in the recognition of a nonrecurring $5.3 million milestone payment for completing certain growth initiatives and (ii) the addition of recurring profit sharing, which was $2.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026. ● Gross profit was $434.3 million, a decrease of $82.8 million, or 16.0%, and total gross margin was 27.4%, a decrease of 119 basis points. The gross profit decrease was mainly driven by the $32.4 million lower new vehicle gross profit, $30.8 million lower finance and insurance, net gross profit, $14.8 million of decreased used vehicle gross profit, and $14.3 million of decreased products, service and other gross profit, partially offset by an $8.0 million increase in Good Sam Club gross profit and a $1.5 million increase in Good Sam Services and Plans gross profit. ● Selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) were $387.1 million, a decrease of $23.9 million, or 5.8%. This decrease was primarily due to a $25.5 million decrease in employee cash compensation costs excluding commissions, resulting primarily from headcount reductions; a $4.2 million decrease in stock-based compensation expense (“SBC”); and a $2.3 million decrease in commission costs, partially offset by a $4.5 million increase in outside service provider fees primarily related to software, AI, and infrastructure maintenance expenses and a $2.5 million increase in rent expense. SG&A Excluding SBC (5) was $383.6 million, a decrease of $19.8 million, or 4.9%. As a percentage of gross profit, SG&A and SG&A Excluding SBC were 89.1% and 88.3%, respectively, an increase of 964 and 1,032 basis points, respectively. ● The Company recorded a noncash goodwill impairment charge of $286.7 million for the third quarter of 2026 related to its RV and Outdoor Retail reporting unit. The charge was largely driven by continued pressure on new RV industry demand, promotional pricing pressure in core travel trailer offerings, and 2 the sustained decline in our share price, as well as macroeconomic factors, including higher consumer interest rates, elevated fuel prices and declines in consumer sentiment, which reduced the Company’s estimate of the fair value of the reporting unit as of September 30, 2026. ● Floor plan interest expense was $15.2 million, a decrease of $2.9 million, or 16.1%, primarily due to a 55 basis point decrease in the average floor plan borrowing rate and an 8.3% decrease in the average floor plan balance. The average interest rate for the Company’s Floor Plan Facility for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was 5.93% and 6.48%, respectively. ● Net loss was $320.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $290.7 million, or 990.5%. Adjusted EBITDA was $36.0 million, a decrease of $59.7 million, or 62.4%. ● Diluted loss per share of Class A common stock was $(3.09), an increase of $2.45, or 382.8%, from $(0.64) for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Adjusted loss per share – diluted (5) of Class A common stock was $(0.19), a change of $0.62, or 144.2%, from Adjusted earnings per share – diluted (5) of Class A common stock of $0.43 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. ● The total number of our store locations was 197 as of September 30, 2026 and 2025. ​ ​ ​ (4) Unless otherwise indicated, all financial comparisons in these third quarter operating highlights compare our financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 to our financial results from the third quarter ended September 30, 2025. Camping World Holdings, Inc., headquartered in Lincolnshire, IL, (together with its subsidiaries) is America’s largest retailer of RVs and related products and services. Through Camping World and Good Sam brands, our vision is to make it easy for everyone to enjoy RVing and empower our customers’ joy of travel. We strive to build long-term value for our customers, employees, and stockholders by combining a unique and comprehensive assortment of RV products and services with a national network of RV dealerships, service centers and customer support centers along with the industry’s most extensive online presence and a highly trained and knowledgeable team of associates serving our customers, the RV lifestyle, and the communities in 3 which we operate. We also believe that our Good Sam organization and family of highly specialized services and plans, including roadside assistance, protection plans and insurance, uniquely enable us to connect with our customers as stewards of an outdoor and recreational lifestyle. With RV sales and service locations in 44 states, Camping World has grown to become the prime destination for everything RV.
